title: Yudhishthira at the lake
word: the whole five years in seven sits
hookLine: four brothers lie by a lake, and a voice says: answer me before you drink
carry: dharma sees death clearly and still chooses fairness
tomorrow: why would an old hymn of creation end with 'or perhaps not'?

lines: A POP QUIZ, ON A BAD DAY.
cards: A pop quiz is bad enough on a good day. Here's a worse one. Four brothers are lying still at the edge of a clear lake: Nakula, Sahadeva, Arjuna, Bhima.
The eldest, Yudhishthira, has come out of the forest looking for them, and he's found them. He's grieving, and he's so thirsty he kneels to drink. Then a voice from the water: don't.
Your brothers drank before answering me. Answer my questions first. So what does he do?

teach.b: He answers. The voice belongs to a yaksha, a spirit of the place, and its questions come fast. What is quicker than the wind?
The mind. What is more numerous than the grass? Thoughts.
Then the one people still repeat.
What is the greatest wonder? Yudhishthira says: day after day, creatures go to the realm of death, and those who remain act as if they will live forever. What could be more wonderful than that?
The yaksha is satisfied, and offers him one brother back. Only one. Bhima is the strong one; Arjuna is the archer.
Either would make sense with a war ahead. Yudhishthira asks for Nakula. My father had two wives, he says, Kunti and Madri.
I'm Kunti's son, and I'm alive. Let Madri have a living son too.
Then the yaksha shows who he is: Dharma, Yudhishthira's own father, and he gives back all four. Here's the teaching.
The test at the lake was a test of dharma itself, right order, doing what's right, and Yudhishthira's two answers show both halves of it.
See clearly: everyone you love will die, and so will you; don't live as if not. Then act rightly: even with a war coming, choose what's fair over what's useful.
Year three of this path was this great story, told as a serial. If one scene had to hold that year, it would be this one.

how: The yaksha's questions are retold in Hindu homes, storytelling and recitations of the Mahabharata's forest book, and readers of the epic often quote the 'greatest wonder' answer.

games.q: what does “the whole five years in seven sits” mean?
o: a final exam of seven questions to finish a course
a vow to meditate every single day for five years
a look back at the whole path, one sit at a time

games.q: the yaksha's questions. tap the pairs.
p: acting as if you'll live forever

s: Yudhishthira asks for Bhima back, because a war is coming
he asks for Nakula, so that Madri, like Kunti, has a living son.
the voice at the lake turns out to be Yudhishthira's own father, Dharma
and once he is satisfied, he gives back all four brothers.
the 'greatest wonder' in the story is the lake itself
it's that people watch others die and still act as if they'll live forever.

games.q: the yaksha offers Yudhishthira one brother back. a war lies ahead. who does he ask for?
games.why: Nakula. his father had two wives; Kunti's son is alive, so let Madri have a living son too. fairness over strength, and then the yaksha, Dharma, gives back all four.

practice: The greatest wonder is acting as if there's always time. So answer it, gently. Say softly, out loud, the name of one person you'd want to hear from you while there's time.
Then say the one plain sentence you'd tell them: a thank-you, an apology, I'm glad you're here. If you pray, you might offer their name to God before you let it go.
Let it hang in the air for a few breaths; it doesn't have to go anywhere yet.

wordCard.voice: The whole five years in seven sits: the path, looked back on one scene at a time. Year three's scene is a lake, a voice, and dharma put to the test.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a yaksha, a spirit of a place; here the voice at the lake, who turns out to be Dharma.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma sees death clearly and still chooses fairness. Year three fits beside one lake. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana (Aranyaka) Parva, the Yaksha Prashna (Ganguli's sections 311–313): the brothers drink and fall; the voice demands answers first; quicker than the wind, the mind; more numerous than grass, thoughts; the greatest wonder; one brother may live; Yudhishthira chooses Nakula for Madri's sake; the yaksha is Dharma and restores all four
